newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly Q1 Zyprexa growth seen strong.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly Q1 Zyprexa growth seen strong.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co is expected Monday to report strong growth in Zyprexa sales and some success in defending the market share of Prozac.
Drug industry analysts expect Lilly to report first quarter earnings of $0.81 per share, up from $0.71 per share in the year-ago period, according to First Call.

Zyprexa, a drug for treating schizophrenia that was approved and launched only last October, will likely achieve worldwide revenues of $100 million for the quarter, said Salomon Brothers pharmaceuticals analyst Robert Uhl.
"That's a real comfort factor for investors," Uhl said.

Prozac -- Lilly's biggest-selling product and the world's most popular anti-depressant -- is holding its own against aggressive new competitors, such as Zoloft from Pfizer Inc and Paxil from SmithKline Beecham Plc.

Growth in Prozac sales has slowed and Paxil, especially, is gobbling up new prescriptions, but analysts said the overall market for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, is growing so fast that Prozac has a long way to go.
Prozac's first-quarter sales comparisons may be difficult for Indianapolis-based Lilly, however, Uhl added.
In the first quarter of 1996, Prozac sales were $578.8 million, up 27 percent from the prior year.
The following three quarters, Prozac sales were up five percent, 10 percent and 17 percent, respectively.
"If Prozac grows at 12 or 13 percent, that's all Lilly needs ... All this is built into the stock already," said independent drug industry analyst Hemant Shah.
Lilly is expected to file with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in June for Evista, a new osteoporosis drug, and later this year for Zyprexa as a bipolar disorder therapy.
Shares in Lilly were off 3/4 to 84-5/8.
